statement_refuted: A universal bound on E_Z ||rho_{Y|Z}||_infinity^(2/3) for every orthogonal split into a three-dimensional spectral component Y and complementary component Z, under only independent original-coordinate input densities bounded by one.
stronger_refutation: For every fixed alpha in (0,1), the same construction makes E_Z ||rho_{Y|Z}||_infinity^alpha unbounded.
construction: In R^4 take v=(1,1,1,1)/2, Y the orthogonal projection onto v-perp, Z=v^T X, f1 the indicator of m separated intervals each of length 1/m, and f2=f3=f4=1_[0,1]. Then the Z density is a union of m disjoint identical packets p_m=(1/m)g_m with ||g_m||_infinity<=3/2, while ||rho_{Y|Z=z}||_infinity=1/p_m(z).
exact_lower_bound: E ||rho_{Y|Z}||_infinity^alpha >= (2m/3)^alpha; at alpha=2/3 this diverges as (2m/3)^(2/3).

partner_result_applied.application: For the same v-perp frame every row leverage is 3/4 and every second-row residual leverage is 2/3, so G_ij=(3/4)(2/3)=1/2 and sum_{k!=i,j}|det A_{ijk}|=|det Lambda|/2 >=1/2 when |det Lambda|>=1. Thus the conditional-moment divergence persists under strong determinant-bank geometry.

scope_note: This refutes only the normalized conditional-density-moment proof interface. It is not a counterexample to the QFORM bounded-density conjecture and does not challenge the exact-rank-three theorem.
replacement_obligation: Keep the unnormalized original product fiber weight coupled to the nonlinear curvature payment, or use a global Fourier/small-ball mechanism before conditional normalization.
